items.label: Barometer, Sep 2026
items.text: The main argument for maintaining our overweight stance on stocks comes down to corporate profitability.

items.label: Barometer, Sep 2026
items.text: Also in stocks’ favour are economic conditions.

items.label: Barometer, Sep 2026
items.text: With corporate earnings growth set to be the main driver of equity outperformance, we favour the sectors and regions that are best placed to deliver those profits.

items.label: Barometer, Sep 2026
items.text: That means maintaining an overweight position in technology stocks.

items.label: Barometer, Sep 2026
items.text: The AI-driven capex boom, and the need for infrastructure to support it, should support the outlook for industrials, another sector on which we have an overweight stance.

items.label: Barometer, Sep 2026
items.text: Although the sector retains defensive characteristics, higher long-term yields mean utilities’ status as a bond proxy and their reliable dividend payments are less attractive.

items.label: Barometer, Sep 2026
items.text: We therefore downgrade utilities to neutral.

items.label: Barometer, Sep 2026
items.text: Regionally, our preference is for emerging-market stocks (excluding China), which continue to benefit from strong global trade flows, elevated commodity prices, favourable growth dynamics, and extensive exposure to the AI theme.

items.label: Barometer, Sep 2026
items.text: Latin American stocks trade at especially attractive valuations, ranking as the cheapest region globally in our model.

items.label: Barometer, Sep 2026
items.text: Although the move has improved valuations for government bonds, we retain our neutral stance on both Treasuries and eurozone sovereign debt.

items.label: Barometer, Sep 2026
items.text: We also favour emerging-market local-currency debt outside China.

items.label: Barometer, Sep 2026
items.text: We remain neutral on bonds and underweight cash.

items.label: Monthly CIO Update, Sep 2026
items.text: We remain positive on equities, with a preference for emerging-market stocks, especially in Asia, where exposure to AI investment is a positive, in our view.

items.label: Monthly CIO Update, Sep 2026
items.text: This is one of the reasons why we’ve upgraded gold to overweight.

items.label: 2026 outlook, Q4 update
items.text: We stay constructive on risk but are increasingly selective, favoring AI bottlenecks, shorter-term bonds and opportunities beyond asset class labels.

items.label: 2026 outlook, Q4 update
items.text: We stay overweight U.S. equities and upgrade emerging market stocks to overweight but stay focused on opportunities driven by bottlenecks.

items.label: 2026 outlook, Q4 update
items.text: We prefer short-term bonds over long-term bonds with high sensitivity to interest rates.

items.label: 2026 outlook, Q4 update
items.text: We remain constructive on AI, while focusing on bottlenecks and infrastructure as financing needs and capital intensity rise.

items.label: 2026 outlook, Q4 update
items.text: We prefer short-term bonds to long-term government bonds, where heavy issuance and term-premium risk can amplify volatility.

items.label: Global Market Outlook, Sep 2026
items.text: The bond yield outlook and renewed momentum in the AI theme are supportive of our Overweight view on US and Asia ex-Japan equities.

items.label: Global Market Outlook, Sep 2026
items.text: We reinstate our Overweight stance on gold as USD weakness resumes.

items.label: Global Market Outlook, Sep 2026
items.text: Continue to favour corporate and EM bonds over G3 government bonds.

items.label: Global Market Outlook, Sep 2026
items.text: We remain Overweight EM USD government bonds due to fiscal fundamentals, but see most corporate and EM bonds as attractive sources of yield.

items.label: Global Market Outlook, Sep 2026
items.text: Softening yield concerns positive for equities A pricing out of Fed rate hike expectations would be supportive for equities; we stay Overweight.

items.label: Global Market Outlook, Sep 2026
items.text: Financial sector an attractive route to broadening exposure.

items.label: Global Market Outlook, Sep 2026
items.text: Financials remain a preferred sector across the US, Euro area and Japan markets.

items.label: Global Market Outlook, Sep 2026
items.text: Notwithstanding our preference for broadening exposure, positive momentum in the technology and AI sectors is expected to resume after around two months of underperformance relative to value -style sectors.

items.label: Global Market Outlook, Sep 2026
items.text: The combination of our bond yield and sector views supports our Overweight views on US and AxJ equities, as well as Core holding views on Japan and the Euro area.

items.label: Global Market Outlook, Sep 2026
items.text: Our Overweight view on China equities remains in place, given increasingly undemanding valuations.

items.label: Global Market Outlook, Sep 2026
items.text: Reinstating gold Overweight as USD weakens We reinstate our Overweight stance on gold .

items.label: Global Market Outlook, Sep 2026
items.text: Together, this argues for reinstating our Overweight gold view.

items.label: Global Market Outlook, Sep 2026
items.text: Statistical revisions to the way some professional services and computer software inflation is measured, due end-September, should retroactively lower the Fed’s preferred core PCE inflation for the past five years , reinforcing the path towards 2% by 2027.

items.label: Global Market Outlook, Sep 2026
items.text: Within the asset class, we maintain an Overweight stance on EM USD government bonds and an Underweight stance on DM government bonds.

items.label: Global Market Outlook, Sep 2026
items.text: We , therefore, favour the 3-5-year part of the curve and credit over duration.

items.label: Global Market Outlook, Sep 2026
items.text: In EM, we continue to favour EM USD over LCY government bonds.

items.label: Global Market Outlook, Sep 2026
items.text: We are Overweight US equities, with fundamental earnings strength and reasonable valuations.

items.label: Global Market Outlook, Sep 2026
items.text: We remain Overweight AxJ equities – a key beneficiary of AI capex, which shows no signs of slowing down.

items.label: Global Market Outlook, Sep 2026
items.text: Within AxJ, we continue to remain Overweight Taiwan, with good visibility on AI-driven growth, and Overweight China for its valuation re-rating potential.

items.label: Global Market Outlook, Sep 2026
items.text: We are positive on the long-term agreements driving the memory chip industry, giving greater visibility to future earnings growth.

items.label: Global Market Outlook, Sep 2026
items.text: Fiscal expansion is lifting domestic demand and benefiting the industrial sector, while higher-for-longer rates favour the banking sector.

items.label: Global Market Outlook, Sep 2026
items.text: Sector views: Continue to broaden & diversify We are Overweight US technology and communication services, which are expected to be the primary drivers of US earnings growth, supported by structural AI tailwinds and broadening AI monetisation.

items.label: Global Market Outlook, Sep 2026
items.text: Beyond tech, we retain a broad Overweight in financials across the US, Europe ex -UK and Japan, whose stable earnings growth profile s underpin our view amid buoyant markets, elevated rates and reasonable valuations.

items.label: Global Market Outlook, Sep 2026
items.text: In addition, we remain Overweight Europe ex-UK industrials, given EU fiscal stimulus, bolstered by Germany's new infrastructure acceleration legislation.

items.label: Global Market Outlook, Sep 2026
items.text: We remain Underweight real estate and consumer staples amid weak sentiment and low visibility on the housing recovery.
